title: The Night Watch — Zombification Arc
premise: Isaac's words: "Continue the story of The Night Watch based on Wystan Ashmore and Malphas which eventually ends with them working at the Aetherion Academy separately without knowing they were connected. This story is called 'The Night Watch — Zombification Arc'. 80 chapters." The book continues from the last line of The Night's Watch. Wystan's gift gets the hand and never the purse, and Article XV prosecutes only the purse; this time he gets the purse (Xu Deming) and never the hand (Malphas). Malphas makes the dose walk: a contractile matrix leaning down a saturation gradient toward the quiet, which is the capped mains, the districts the Accord cuts at night, and the lowest-saturation body in a room, which is Wystan. The case closes on Deming by Accord law; the hand is named in no file Wystan can read; the official classification stays bleed. Years later both men teach at the Aetherion Academy in separate wings, and neither ever learns of the other.

chapters.title: The Docket Head
chapters.beat: Picking up the second she finishes writing her name at the head of the docket, Wystan strikes the fresh tin's wax with his brass, enters the Ferriby wedge as Register exhibit one, and folds the four chapter-wax pieces into a paper he dates on the outside. He writes to Tally for a second dataset and the name of whoever set the marker, and sends Yinzhi home. At the sixth division the main comes back and the hum fills the building; he carries the tin to the day desk, finds Brack's classification entered and closed, and enters his own memorandum beneath it, one word in the margin: edges. The Ferriby filing is now a Register file with an exhibit and a named assay, and nobody on the day desk reads past the classification.
chapters.place: Cutler Row, the Night Register (the scullery back room) and the day desk at the sixth division
chapters.time_elapsed: The same night, from the fourth division to the sixth

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Drops
chapters.beat: The ninth hind lies on the table by the second division and Vesk builds the contractile matrix into his third-dilution formulation, flask in both palms because his hands will not close. Nuvalik opens the shoulder and will not say what she found in the fourth hind; Malphas sits on the gauge bench in the four-degree cold with his fingers the colour of a living man's and asks Foss to get him the Arbitration Division's field manual. Vesk counts the drip, twenty-two a minute, and lets the question of what Stage the Lord is go by again. The work turns from proving rot to making it move.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse
chapters.time_elapsed: Day 1; the second division to the ninth

chapters.title: The Morning Check
chapters.beat: Wystan wakes at noon with his hands shaking, reads Keld's minute against the written record as he does every morning, and walks to the medical house where Keld sits at a window still waiting for a relief that came too late. At the day desk Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle reads the edges memorandum and tells him the Register may keep a curiosity open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing and not a day longer. Brack stops him in the corridor, stands by his classification, and hands over the Bureau's raw readings unasked; in Lyle's closed room Wystan feels the day's residue settle on his skin as it always does and does not remark it. He knows he will get a hand and not a purse, and says so to Brack in those words.
chapters.place: the Division's medical house and the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk
chapters.time_elapsed: Day 1; noon to the ninth division

chapters.title: A Number in the Room
chapters.beat: In the Xu counting house by the river Deming draws the second tranche of Verdantia off the Swale supply contract as wastage and writes the covering letter as ordered, naming Project Zombification in the second line. He counts the days Malphas has given him and the weeks the Logistics return will take, and argues with a Logistics factor over a column he intends to lie in. He tells the factor the Hollow Shaft story as a joke about careless men; it is the thing he is most afraid of. The purse now has paper on it, in his hand, carrying the chosen word.
chapters.place: the Xu counting house by the river

chapters.title: Who Set the Marker
chapters.beat: Tally's answer comes up with the bulletin bundle: the marker is the Ferriby estate's old survey stone. Wystan and Yinzhi ride to the cut, where Tally (first seen, first inventoried) walks them the line, and Wystan stands eight hours on the carcass ground without food to run Called Late on a scene weeks cold. He states a sequence: somebody came up from the south along the estate's round, stopped short of the stone, and went back the way he came, on foot, at a walking pace, more than once. The inquiry moves off the cut and onto the round.
chapters.place: the North Ferriby cut and the parish marker

chapters.title: Separately
chapters.beat: In the ice-press room Malphas has the discussion he promised: Nuvalik says she hid the twitch in the fourth hind's shoulder because a thing that twitches is a thing that will walk, and he asks her to make it happen again by morning. Foss reads the Division field manual aloud, the unsigned paragraph on anamnetic reading and its counters: seal the object, use an intermediary, wait a season, move a wall. Malphas makes each counter a house rule (every flask Fixatio-sealed, no live dose touched bare, everything through a second pair of hands) and tells Foss that when the work is done he will be released with his own name. The cell now works against the Night Register as against a form it has read.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse, the ice-press room

chapters.title: The Lick-Keeper
chapters.beat: On the estate round Wystan finds the salt licks, one every half mile, the last twenty-two paces short of the marker, and the lick-keeper Josse Garretsohn, who says the estate steward paid for the new tonic blocks. Wystan takes a block bare-handed and receives his forty-third minute: Josse setting it, content, nobody else anywhere in it. The far side of the marker was clean because the round stopped there and the carrier turned home; the carrier is Josse, and Josse is an intermediary. Wystan has the hand, and the hand is the wrong one.
chapters.place: the Ferriby estate lick round

chapters.title: Rounding
chapters.beat: Foss rides to the Swale road inn to meet the carter who meets the carter who supplies Josse, and pays him in salt bars because salt bars leave no bill. The carter mentions that a man from the Register has asked the Ferriby lick-keeper about blocks. Foss carries it back; Malphas stops Ferriby for a season and moves the licks to the Swale walks, and Foss spends the ride home rehearsing the explanation he still gives about a rounding convention. The dosing network loses one route and gains a wider one.
cast: a carter on the Swale road
chapters.place: the Swale road inn and Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: Two Myriads
chapters.beat: In the Division archive Wystan works the metered-draw tariff by hand and arrives at the price of third-dilution Verdantia against nine hinds and a stag: two myriads and a fraction. He petitions Logistics and Supply for the draw records of the Swale line and three others and is refused on the nine-word wire: returns publish on the schedule and not before. At the Timberline chapter bench Yinzhi reproduces a threshold compound that is inert in the flask and runs in blood. Wystan files a standing request against the Swale line so that the day the return publishes it lands on his desk.
cast: a Logistics clerk on the wire
chapters.place: the Division archive and the Timberline chapter bench

chapters.title: The Ninth Hind
chapters.beat: At night in the coldhouse the ninth hind, dead twenty-three days, stands up off the table and leans across the slate toward the capped standpipe housing in the corner, where Malphas has been sitting on the gauge bench; he rises and walks to the door before she reaches it, and Vesk takes it for courtesy. She lies down against the housing and stays down. Deming, present to hear what his money bought, is sick in the yard; Foss writes the distance and the time; Malphas says the sink is the quiet. The matrix walks.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: Salt
chapters.beat: The licks are watched, so Malphas wants the dose in salt bars, and Deming's lineage holds the parish-relief contract that pays the Wicket Lane poor in salt bars, money that can be eaten. Deming works out what salt in a parish means and does it anyway, over a meal he does not eat, with his thumb going round his hat brim. He moves the relief contract's next delivery to a press Foss built. The dose is now in currency.
chapters.place: the Xu counting house and the parish-relief warehouse

chapters.title: The Memorandum
chapters.beat: At the full desk Wystan argues edges before Lyle, Brack and the day clerks with the lick round drawn on the board and Josse's minute in the file. Brack concedes the edge is real and holds that the classification is still correct: the residue is the deer's, and a deer cannot be charged. Lyle gives Wystan until the quarterly inspection to produce a purse, and enters the edges memorandum as the Register's position. The file has a stated theory with his name on it.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: Release
chapters.beat: On a ridge above the Swale walks at night Nuvalik watches hinds that took the dosed licks die standing, then, days later, get up and walk downhill into the dark, not running, leaning. Nobody from the cell has touched a lick; the carter's man set them and has gone. She thinks about the sky and the ground, and about the three people whose name she carries. The dead are loose and nobody but the cell knows it yet.
chapters.place: a ridge above the Swale walks

chapters.title: The One That Walked
chapters.beat: Tally walks his line again, as Wystan asked, and in the Swale walks finds a hind lying eleven miles from any lick at a Withering-cut hamlet with a dead standpipe, and then, at dusk, sees one walking. He measures what he can with a rule, follows it until it lies down, writes the time, and finds no line anywhere he could stand and check the far side of. He carries the insert himself again and the clerk sends it to the Night Register.
chapters.place: the Swale walks and a Withering-cut hamlet

chapters.title: No Edge
chapters.beat: With Tally's insert in his coat Wystan walks the Swale walks with Yinzhi and Tally and finds carcasses spread across fifty miles in no pattern the edges theory can hold. He touches a walked hind bare and gets his forty-fourth minute: nobody in it, only downhill, only content, a leaning with no one leaning. He writes it down exactly and has no reading for it. The file's theory is broken in the field before anyone at the desk knows.
chapters.place: the Swale walks

chapters.title: The Weather Form
chapters.beat: Brack re-classifies the Swale carcasses off true measurements, bleed, Verdantia, no operator, no edge, and he is right by the instrument. Lyle reads the Register's edges memorandum aloud against it before the whole desk, and the day clerks laugh in the way clerks laugh. Wystan strikes edges in his day book with one line so it can still be read, and writes bleed beside it in quotation marks. The Register's position is withdrawn in public.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: Eleven Miles
chapters.beat: The cell tallies the walks off the Society's inserts and the Bureau's published returns, and Malphas reads the re-classification and is satisfied. Vesk's second graft is failing; the nails come in faster, and he is offered a third graft and refuses it because his fingers would be shorter again. Foss notes that the walks run eleven miles and four to six days, exactly as said. The released work now looks like weather to the one office that measures it.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: Relief
chapters.beat: At the medical house Keld calls Wystan by the name of the officer who should have relieved them, and Wystan answers to it. Keld's minute holds against the written record. Yinzhi finds him there with a coil: the Swale lie-down points all read near floor ambient, and she wants to know what the Accord cut near each of them. The file gains its next question.
chapters.place: the Division's medical house

chapters.title: Wastage
chapters.beat: A Logistics clerk, Nella Stower, queries the Swale column early on the wire and Deming answers her in person with a pumping-array fault report he has had forged; she believes him and enters the query closed. Walking home he understands why every letter he writes must carry the project's name and his own hand. He counts: nineteen days of usefulness left.
chapters.place: the Logistics and Supply returns desk

chapters.title: The Hollow Shaft File
chapters.beat: Wystan draws the Hollow Shaft file from the archive: a cell convicted twenty years ago off one name in private correspondence, the payer amerced to ruin, the hand never found. He reads how the file was built, writ by writ, from a single letter, and copies the procedure into his day book. He notes the file has no Anamnetic exhibit at all. The Register has a precedent for convicting a purse off paper.
chapters.place: the Division archive

chapters.title: Map of the Quiet
chapters.beat: Yinzhi lays every lie-down point against the Accord's registers of capped mains, dead legs and Withering-cut hamlets, and every one sits at a quiet place. She walks the arithmetic to Wystan in sequence and leaves the result to the end: they go downhill in saturation, toward the quiet. She notices he goes very still at the word quiet and does not ask why. The file now has a mechanism in it that is not Wystan's.
chapters.place: the Timberline chapter bench and Cutler Row, the Night Register (the scullery back room)

chapters.title: The Thirty-First Day
chapters.beat: On the thirty-first day Malphas tells Deming he is not needed at the coldhouse again and hands him the last bundle of letters to post, every one naming the Project. Deming posts them. He works out on the walk back that the name funnels to him, and that if he names the hand he becomes a witness the hand must remove; he decides that whatever the Accord asks he will not give it the hand. His usefulness has been counted to the day.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse and the post

chapters.title: The Gradient
chapters.beat: At a Withering-cut hamlet with a capped standpipe Wystan and Yinzhi put a recovered hind in a sealed barn and watch it lean toward the quietest corner. Wystan explains the gradient in the Technical Register, contractile tissue leaning down a saturation gradient to a sink; Yinzhi sees the lean shift when he moves and he says it is the draught. They have the physics and not the author.
chapters.place: a Withering-cut hamlet at the Swale head

chapters.title: What the Sky Does
chapters.beat: Nuvalik walks the Swale walks alone to see the dead hamlets and finds the ravens still sitting in the trees, not coming down. On the far ridge a man is measuring a carcass with a rule, and she knows the name Malphas said; she could walk down and tell him to stop eating the lick salt he carries in his pack, and she does not. The watchers are now inside the work's ground.
chapters.place: the Swale walks

chapters.title: Downhill
chapters.beat: In the city a walking hind comes in off the north road after the eleventh division and lies down against the Register's own outer stair on Cutler Row. Wystan reads it as a message: the formulator knows the Register sits in the quiet and is walking the dead to its door. Yinzhi hears the theory and does not argue. The Register now believes it is being answered.
chapters.place: Cutler Row, the outer stair, after the eleventh division

chapters.title: Precedent
chapters.beat: Wystan asks Lyle to open an Article XV purse file against the Swale line before the return, citing Hollow Shaft; she refuses him (no ledger, no purse) and tells him the Enforcement Division has asked for every carcass report. Wystan understands that the dead have become someone else's jurisdiction as well as his. Lyle signs the reports over.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: The Human Question
chapters.beat: Malphas tells the cell that deer spend in six days and a man is bigger, and that the salt bars have been in the Wicket Lane parish a turn. Foss argues the Oath way, in clauses; Vesk is delighted; Nuvalik says nothing and wipes her knife. Foss builds the second salt press because he is the one who can. The project takes human substrate.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: The Fever Parish
chapters.beat: The Wicket Lane layer-out, Greta, sends to the Society because her dead do not smell, and Wystan comes. In the death-house nine dead lie in the sitting, salt bars in their purses; he touches a bar and gets his forty-fifth minute, the parish relief clerk counting them out, nobody else. Brack, called, says the parish had fever before any of this. The dose has a door into people.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish, the death-house

chapters.title: The Pit
chapters.beat: From the lane at night Vesk and Foss watch the paupers' pit at Wicket Lane, where the excluded go without the roll, and see the dead climb out of the lime and walk into the cut district, slow, unafraid. Vesk remembers the stones on the graves in his village and laughs out loud. The salt bar has done what the flask did.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish, the paupers' pit

chapters.title: In Registro
chapters.beat: At first light Wystan walks the cut district and counts the parish dead lying in doorways where they lay down at the quietest points of the street. Greta cannot enter them in the roll because they were excluded; the Enforcement carts arrive before the layer-out can sit a single shift with them. Wystan writes each face into his day book because nobody else will. Human dead have walked, and the Accord has noticed.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish and the cut district

chapters.title: Upper Bailiff
chapters.beat: Upper Bailiff Aldric Harrow of the Enforcement Division takes the dead as a public-safety matter and claims them as forfeitures in Lyle's room, and Arbitration and Enforcement have the argument they have had for two hundred years. Harrow is one of the two Enforcement men who once made Wystan drop his Domain by threatening what stood outside it, and he mentions it pleasantly. Lyle gives Harrow the streets and keeps the file.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: Night Cut
chapters.beat: Yinzhi learns that Lyle handed her gradient map to Harrow and that Enforcement is cutting the poorer districts at night, on purpose, to draw the dead away from the chartered ones. She stands at a gauge-housing as an inspector caps a death-house's line in Wicket Lane though Article XX forbids it, and he tells her the exemption is claimed far more often than it is granted. Her map has become a design for pens.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish

chapters.title: The Hall Asks
chapters.beat: The Xu hall senior asks Deming why the parish-relief contract has been delivering from a new press, and Deming tells him a supplier changed, which is true and not the answer. His uncle lets it go for the length of the meal. Deming counts the weeks to the return: four.
chapters.place: the Xu lineage hall

chapters.title: A Desk with a Brass Token
chapters.beat: Malphas reads Enforcement's night cuts as a gift: the Accord is building his sinks for him. He asks Foss who the Night Register is, and Foss, after two days asking at inns, reports a desk on Cutler Row with a brass token and a man on nights; Malphas says then it is a desk, and designs the next release around the cut districts. The walks now run fourteen miles.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: STAY
chapters.beat: In a Wicket lodging room a dead man is getting up, halfway through the contraction, and Wystan seals the room and seats STAY so that the working stops mid-run and every operation in the room is recorded. It is the first live exhibit of the mechanism anyone has held. Inside it he cannot strike, seal or open a door; he stands in the thick air with the noise of the street arriving late, and waits for Brack.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish, a lodging room

chapters.title: Outside the Boundary
chapters.beat: Harrow arrives first, with fire, and the lodging family is on the stair outside the boundary as the district goes dark and the dead start down the lane; he says he will leave them outside the cordon unless Wystan drops the Domain. Wystan drops it. Harrow's men burn the room and the exhibit in it, and the family is walked out. The Register loses its live evidence to the one counter his Domain has.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish

chapters.title: Forty Miles a Week
chapters.beat: Tally walks the Ferriby line for the dataset, measuring, with the lick salt he has carried and eaten for two months in his pack. At dusk he goes down in the cut with a broken ankle, writes the day's figures in his notebook with the rule laid across the page, and gets cold, then warm, then content. He dies there counting.
chapters.place: the North Ferriby cut

chapters.title: The Sky Refuses
chapters.beat: The carter brings word that a forester lay two days in the Ferriby cut and no raven came down to him, and then that he was gone. Nuvalik goes to the cut against the rule and finds his rule where he fell, and understands what her proverb was always about: when the sky refuses, people walk out to see why, and now the dead walk out too. She keeps the rule.
cast: a carter on the Swale road
chapters.place: the North Ferriby cut

chapters.title: Eleventh Division
chapters.beat: Harrow orders Cutler Row cut at the eleventh division as the pen for the Wicket dead, the Register's street, because the gradient map says it will draw. Wystan will not leave the Register's rooms; Yinzhi will not leave him. They sit through the last of the hum and hear it stop.
chapters.place: Cutler Row

chapters.title: Cutler Row
chapters.beat: The dead come down Cutler Row in the dark, deer and parish dead and a forester with no rule in his coat, and Enforcement's cordon burns them at the lane mouths. Yinzhi, at the window, sees them pass every quiet doorway and come to the Register's door and lie down at Wystan's feet where he stands on the step. She sees Tally among them and knows him by his coat.
chapters.place: Cutler Row, after the eleventh division

chapters.title: The Second Dataset
chapters.beat: In the aftermath Wystan takes Tally's notebook out of Tally's coat: the second dataset from the same observer, complete to the night he died, last line in his hand. Wystan has stood all night on the lowest ground in the street and taken in everything the dead carried, and in the morning Keld's minute does not match the written record by one word. He writes the discrepancy down and does not correct it.
chapters.place: Cutler Row, the Night Register (the scullery back room)

chapters.title: Forfeiture
chapters.beat: Harrow claims the Cutler Row dead as forfeitures and burns them without the roll; Wystan, before Lyle, gets one name entered: Nol Tally, Timberline chapter, North Ferriby walk. Arbitration loses the rest. The Register's street was a pen and the Division has minuted it as a success.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: Graft
chapters.beat: Vesk's grafts were grown on his own Verdantia, and the ferment has been in his hands for a year; the nails will not stop. Malphas examines him from a pace off, gloved, and does not touch, and Vesk sees for the first time that the Lord never touches anything live. He asks Nuvalik, when it comes, for stones.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: Low Ground
chapters.beat: In the Register's back room, a sealed volume, Brack and Yinzhi move a recovered walker's cage from wall to wall and the dead thing leans each time toward Wystan wherever he stands. Brack reads his Shell as the lowest saturation in the room; Wystan says his own trait aloud, Low Ground, and understands that nobody sent the dead to his door. He is the sink, and the formulator does not know he exists.
chapters.place: Cutler Row, the Night Register (the scullery back room)

chapters.title: Stones
chapters.beat: Vesk dies in the coldhouse with his hands in a basin, counting the drip, thinking of the stones on the graves in his village and the question he asked as a boy. His last pleasure is that he will find out.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: What the Ground Starts
chapters.beat: In the night Vesk's body stands up off the pallet and leans toward the capped standpipe in the corner, and Nuvalik lays stones on it, one on each hand and one on the chest, the way his village did. Malphas has Foss measure the lean before she finishes. Nuvalik understands what her grafted friend asked for and why the stones were always there.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.beat: Eleven weeks to the day the Logistics return publishes, and Wystan's standing request drops it on his desk: the Swale line, a pumping array with four years of flat wastage, has had a bad spring. Nella Stower's closed query is in the margin. The purse has a column.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: The Column
chapters.beat: Deming reads the same return in the counting house and his uncle reads it over his shoulder. Nothing can be burned; the letters were posted a turn and a half ago. He sits with his hat on his knee and waits for the knock he predicted.
chapters.place: the Xu counting house

chapters.title: Article XV
chapters.beat: Wystan opens the Article XV purse file and argues the doctrine before Lyle: a working run by an animal's Lattice has no author in its own grammar, like a spoken one, so liability falls on the payer. Lyle grants the file for its life because Harrow wants the Swale contract's forfeiture and needs a conviction to get it. Wystan and Harrow now want the same verdict for opposite reasons.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: Wait a Season
chapters.beat: Malphas stops all releases and tells the cell to wait a season. The letters naming the Project are already in the world, and he lets Deming fall: the file will be built off a word he chose. Foss understands that the name was always a funnel to one man.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.beat: Wystan builds the file from paper: the Swale return, the relief contract's delivery book, the carter's inn account, and the first of Deming's letters obtained by writ to the post office under the Hollow Shaft procedure. Every thread converges on the Xu counting house and every letter names the Project. He touches no exhibit; there is no hand on paper.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk and the post office

chapters.title: The Hall Decides
chapters.beat: The Xu hall senior strikes Deming's standing ahead of any charge and, without telling him, hires a knife to recover the letters from the Register. Deming learns it at the door when his key no longer turns. He sits on the counting-house step with his hat in his hands.
chapters.place: the Xu lineage hall

chapters.title: Knife
chapters.beat: The knife-man comes into the Register at the fourth division for the letters, and Wystan draws the arming sword for the fifth time on the desk. He is weak against any competent man with a knife and takes a cut through the left forearm and another under the ribs, and keeps the letters; the man goes out the scullery window. Yinzhi finds him sitting on the floor with the letter case held by its edge.
cast: a knife-man hired by the Xu hall
chapters.place: Cutler Row, the Night Register (the scullery back room)

chapters.title: Recovery
chapters.beat: Yinzhi sits the wound and reads the letters while he sleeps: every one names Project Zombification and none names a hand. When he wakes feverish he tells her the purse will name the hand under reservation; she does not believe it and does not say so. She sees the shape of the funnel and he does not.
chapters.place: Cutler Row, the Night Register (the scullery back room)

chapters.title: The Last Name
chapters.beat: Nuvalik sets down the name she has worn in the cell and leaves Greyshaft Nine with Tally's rule and nothing else. She informs no one; Malphas lets her go and says she owes him nothing he wrote down. She walks north under her Accord roll-name to where the name came from.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse and the north road

chapters.title: Writ
chapters.beat: The Bench issues the writ and Wystan, wound bound, goes with Harrow's men to the Xu counting house. Deming comes out with his hat in his hands and says he said this would happen before it happened. The payer is in custody.
chapters.place: the Xu counting house

chapters.title: The Word
chapters.beat: The Bench clerk titles the file In re Project Zombification, and Wystan, preparing testimony with Yinzhi and Brack, sees that every thread ends in the word and none goes past it. The word is the only author the file has. He files it anyway because it is the only purse he has ever held.
chapters.place: the Bench of Attribution, the northern sitting hall, the clerks' room

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.beat: On the first day of the sitting Deming's advocate says the Ferriby exhibit was tampered with, because a quarter inch of growth inside a sealed Fixatio tin is impossible. Yinzhi, the assay of record, says Fixatio holds what it is given and it was given a running working; Wystan lays the four chapter-wax pieces on the glass and they fit the join. The Ruling chair reads the Hollow Shaft precedent into the record and Deming lifts his head at the name.
chapters.place: the Bench of Attribution, the northern sitting hall
chapters.time_elapsed: Day 112, a sitting on Uurgath's day

chapters.title: The Register Is a Person
chapters.beat: Deming watches the Night Register testify: a thin man in black who holds the file by its edge and says exactly what he cannot attribute. The chairs take the analogy to the spoken working two to one, the Doctrine chair's dissent entered in full, and Deming's advocate has nothing left but the hour. Deming understands he will be convicted before dinner and that the question after it will be the hand.
chapters.place: the Bench of Attribution, the northern sitting hall

chapters.title: The Gallery
chapters.beat: At the afternoon sitting the verdict is read on the Register's file, no officer named aloud: Deming convicted as payer, amercement set to his means, which is everything, and his standing reserved until he names the hand. While it is read Wystan notices a man in the gallery whose hands keep a living colour in a hall where every other pair has gone white, notes it the way he notes a faulty gutter, and returns to the dock. The Ruling chair asks Deming for the hand; Deming looks up at the gallery once, where forty people sit, and refuses, and is taken down.
chapters.place: the Bench of Attribution, the northern sitting hall

chapters.title: Reserved
chapters.beat: Wystan has the purse and not the hand, the inverse of his whole career, and Harrow is already seizing the Swale contract. Greta sends word: the fever's dead lie in the Wicket death-house and Harrow has ordered the district cut tonight, death-house and all. The last salt is still in the parish.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk and the Bench steps

chapters.title: Death-House
chapters.beat: Wystan brings the families of the Wicket dead inside the death-house before dark, so that nothing they love stands outside any boundary he might draw, and seals the volume. Harrow's cordon forms in the lane with fire. The main goes off.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish, the death-house

chapters.title: The Quiet Man
chapters.beat: Wystan lets his suppression go for the first time in years and seats STAY at full in the death-house, and the Pressure of a Stage X Master comes off him into the lane and drops the cordon to its knees. Harrow tries the counter again and finds nothing of Wystan's outside; the dead stop mid-lean, and Greta enters every one of them on the parish roll by name while the working holds. At dawn Wystan releases it and has taken in everything the room carried.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish, the death-house

chapters.title: Six
chapters.beat: At dawn Yinzhi holds Wystan up in the lane while the cordon picks itself off the stones. Everyone in it knows now what Stage he is; the six who knew are not six any more, and by noon the Division has it in writing. She walks him home by the long way through a district with its main on.
chapters.place: Wicket Lane fever parish and the road to Cutler Row

chapters.title: Disciplinary
chapters.beat: Lyle enters a disciplinary observation: a Master concealing his Stage from his own Division. The Register's standing goes under review and Wystan answers every question he is asked and none he is not. He sits the length of it with his hands on his knees to hide the shaking.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: Substrate
chapters.beat: Malphas ends the project: the supply is cut with Deming reserved and the substrate spent. He has Foss move the coldhouse's partition wall a yard and the rail with it before they go, and they burn the flasks in the ice-press room. Greyshaft Nine is left with its drip and its cold.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: Bleed
chapters.beat: The Accord's official classification of the walking dead stays bleed, and Brack signs it again, correctly, off true measurements: no operator indicated. Lyle explains to Wystan that the Division will not admit made dead because it would have to admit the night cuts. The one exhibit convicted one payer; everything else is weather.
chapters.place: the Arbitration Division's northern office, the day desk

chapters.title: The Desk Is Folded
chapters.beat: On the last night the carter brings word that the Night Register is being folded into the day desk. Malphas says then the person has gone somewhere else and draws a line through the entry in his book; he gives Foss a sealed purse and his own name back. A letter lies unopened on the gauge bench in a woman's hand Foss does not know, asking whether the question of soil has an answer.
cast: a carter on the Swale road
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse

chapters.title: Returned
chapters.beat: The Bench reserves the attribution of the hand (the power of reservation: not condemned, not closed) and returns the exhibits to the filing party, the Timberline chapter. Yinzhi takes back the Ferriby tin and the four pieces of chapter wax on the chapter's behalf. Wystan signs the release with the pen off the bench.
chapters.place: the Bench of Attribution, the northern sitting hall

chapters.title: Rounding Convention
chapters.beat: Foss takes a bench in a northern coil-shop under his own name, makes honest coils, and writes a petition to the Hexagonal Oath he does not send. He informs no one. He goes on living.
chapters.place: a coil-shop in a northern foundry town

chapters.title: Called Late
chapters.beat: The Swale delivery addresses take Wystan to Greyshaft Nine, burned out and dripping, and he stands fourteen hours to reconstruct it. He states the sequence confidently and articulately: one formulator, working alone, at a bench against the east wall, taking in no visitor; the wall was moved and the sequence is wrong. He files it.
chapters.place: Greyshaft Nine, the coldhouse, burned

chapters.title: Brass
chapters.beat: Wystan reads Keld's minute at Keld's bedside against the written record, and with Keld breathing in the room it comes back word for word. The Night Register is folded and he hands in the brass token he never asked to have changed, refuses the day desk, and takes the Night Watch Society's post as field man; the Society's secretary mentions that the academies ask for field instruction. Yinzhi takes the Timberline chapter bench as its assayer.
chapters.place: the medical house and the Society's bulletin office

chapters.title: Doctor Salter
chapters.beat: Nine years on, Doctor Osric Salter keeps the west-range stillroom at the Aetherion Academy, the one room in the building on a capped dead leg where the hum stops. He teaches preservation and applied ferment to Licentiates, and reads the notice that the Night Watch Society will send a field instructor to Class X this week as he reads weather. His hands are warm on a cold retort.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, the west-range stillroom
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; the first week of Class X

chapters.title: East
chapters.beat: Wystan arrives at the Aetherion Academy as the Society's field man, the Ferriby tin in his satchel under the chapter's wax, and cannot sleep on a building that hums in every wall. Walking the ground at night he finds the one door where the hum stops, the west range, stands at it a moment, and turns back east. His rooms are off the eastern lecture halls.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, the eastern halls and the west-range door
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; two days into Class X's first week

chapters.title: Preservation
chapters.beat: Salter teaches a class to hold a ferment at the edge of running and not over it, and demonstrates with a sealed jar that holds what it was given. A Licentiate asks whether the dead can be kept; Salter says everything can be kept if you do not touch it. He writes the day's word in his course book.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, the west-range stillroom
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; the same day

chapters.title: Hand and Purse
chapters.beat: Mu-jin brings Wystan to Class X, says the Night's Watch man is here, and steps back to the wall. Wystan puts the Ferriby tin on the bench under its chapter wax, does not open it, and teaches attribution from it: you will get the hand, or you will get the purse, and you will never get both. The class is a room of faces that do not decide anything.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, an eastern lecture hall
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; three days into the week

chapters.title: Field Work
chapters.beat: Wystan takes the class out to a real case, a cold scene in the Academy grounds a groundsman reported, and makes them count before they touch. Investigation and inquiry into active magical events, field work, real cases: what their homeroom teacher promised them. He shows them that the scene gives up a hand and nothing more, and names the careless first-year to nobody.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy grounds
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; four days into the week

chapters.title: Across the Quad
chapters.beat: From the west-range window Salter sees a tall man on the east gallery holding a cup by its rim with two fingers, the way nobody holds a cup. He notes it and returns to the jar on his bench. Nothing follows.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, the west-range window
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; five days into the week

chapters.title: West Range
chapters.beat: On his last evening before the Open Tournament clears the timetable Wystan walks the Academy ground again, and at the west-range door the hum stops again. He stands in the quiet a count of ten, the way he stood on Cutler Row with the main off, and turns east. He writes the time in his day book and packs the tin.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, the west-range door and the eastern halls
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; the eve of the Open Tournament

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.beat: In the west-range stillroom Salter fills a fresh specimen jar, lays the lid on, and seals the join with wax. He presses the wax down with the ball of his thumb and sets the jar on the shelf with the others.
chapters.place: the Aetherion Academy, the west-range stillroom
chapters.time_elapsed: Nine years on; the same night

hooks.text: Tally found clean ground on the far side of the parish marker, twenty-two paces past the last carcass, and checked it twice; Wystan writes 'ask Tally who set the marker'. Paid when the lick-keeper's round is found to end at the marker: the carrier turned home there.

A quarter inch of new growth inside a Fixatio-anchored tin with the seal unbroken; the day book reads 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'. Paid at the hearing: Fixatio held what it was given, and what it was given was a running working.
'They are chapter wax and I will want them later.' Four pieces of the broken seal, dated and kept. Paid at the hearing: the pieces fit the join and prove custody.
Wystan asks Tally to keep walking and measuring: 'I want a second dataset from the same observer.' Paid when the notebook is taken from Tally's walking body, complete to the night he died.
The bulletin clerk told Tally the Night Register was a person. The cell knows its hunter only as the Night Register. Paid when the Register is folded and Malphas closes the line.
Wystan holds everything by the very edge, two-fingered, even a cup. Paid in VI: Salter sees a man holding a cup that way across the quad, notes it, and nothing follows.
Malphas's hands keep a living man's colour in a four-degree coldhouse. Paid in the hearing gallery, at the verdict, as a detail Wystan notices and never explains; never recognition.
Nuvalik got contraction out of the fourth hind's shoulder twice and did not report it; Malphas 'will discuss with her separately'. Paid when the discussion happens.
Nuvalik carries a name three people carried before her and thinks she has spent all three on this work. Paid when she sets down the name she wears in the cell and leaves; she does not inform.

Vesk's grafted fingers, the ridged yellow nails that will not stop growing; the village that put stones on its graves. Paid when he dies of his own formulation and Nuvalik lays stones on his walking body.
'Where I was raised, the sky finishes what the ground starts, and when the sky refuses, people walk out to see why.' Paid when the ravens will not come down to Tally and he walks.
Keld's minute, taken off a door handle, lucid, waiting for relief; checked every morning against a written record. It slips by a word after Cutler Row; paid when it is set right at Keld's bedside.

Wystan's Shell rests near zero saturation; free residue in a closed volume runs toward him. The dead lean to the quiet. He believes they are being sent to him; paid when he learns he is the sink and nobody sent them.
The Register token is brass, not silver, because the Night Register is not a full desk, and he has never asked to have it changed. Paid when he hands it in.
Suppression held waking and sleeping; six people alive know what Stage he is. Paid when he drops it in the death-house and the whole cordon knows.
Deming: thirty-one days of usefulness left, and Malphas has already counted them. Paid on the thirty-first day.
'In eleven weeks somebody in a room in the capital will look at the Swale line and see a bad spring.' Paid when the Logistics return publishes.
'I would prefer the file be built off a word I chose.' Every letter names Project Zombification. Paid when the Bench titles the file by the word and every thread ends in it.
'That is how they found the Hollow Shaft people. They found a name in a private correspondence.' Paid when the precedent is read into the record at Deming's hearing.

Foss reads the Division field manual's unsigned paragraph on anamnetic reading and its counters; Malphas adopts them as house rules. Paid when a moved wall makes Wystan's Called Late at Greyshaft Nine confidently wrong.
'The ninth hind is the freshest and she is the one I want.' Paid when she stands up off the table and leans to the standpipe.
Foss pays the carter in salt bars because salt bars leave no bill; the salt bar is money that can be eaten. Paid when the parish dead walk out of the pit with the bars in their purses.
Wystan's margin note: edges. Paid when the walkers erase them and he strikes the word in public.
Brack's classification: Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, no operator indicated, correct off a true measurement. Paid when the Accord's official classification stays bleed and Brack signs it again.
STAY's counter: threaten something outside the boundary; two Enforcement men have used it. Harrow is one. Paid when Wystan drops STAY to save the family on the stair.
Article XX: a death-house may not be cut; the exemption is claimed far more often than granted. Paid when Wystan holds the Wicket death-house under STAY and the dead are entered on the roll.
Deming decides that whatever the Accord asks he will not give it the hand. Paid when the Ruling chair asks and he refuses under reservation.
Malphas promises Foss release with his own name when the work is done. Paid when Foss takes a bench under his own name and informs no one.
When the Bench reserves the hand, the exhibits return to the filing party: the Ferriby tin and the chapter wax go back to Timberline. Paid when the tin is the lesson at Aetherion.

The Society tells Wystan the academies ask for field instruction; at Aetherion, Mu-jin has promised Class X the Night's Watch for 'field work, real cases'. Paid when Wystan takes the class to a real case.
At the Aetherion the hum stops at one door, the west range; Wystan stands there and turns back east. Paid when he does it again at the end of the week and goes no further.
His technique gets the hand, never the purse; Article XV prosecutes only the purse. This case inverts it. Paid when he teaches it: the hand or the purse, never both.

voice_note: The archive crossed between two rooms in three scenes; the book keeps both sides on one calendar and one clock, and each side sees the other only as a form. The Register never has a face for the cell and the Lord never has a name for the Register, and nothing noticed across that line is ever paid as recognition; the narration never winks at the reader who knows both. Wystan-side chapters run in the Register's idiom: numbers, not adjectives; the division of the hour; the day book's margin; one object handled per chapter (tin, block, bar, ledger, wax). Crew chapters run in their POV's craft (Vesk's formulation, Nuvalik's knife, Foss's instruments, Deming's columns), and Malphas is seen, never entered, until Movement VI. The hum and the moment it stops is the book's clock. The dead are reported flat. Exemplar: The main came back at the sixth division and the building filled with it from the floor up. Wystan heard it arrive under the boards and his shoulders came down half an inch. He wrote the time in the margin. The tin sat on the sill under his brass, and the four pieces of chapter wax lay beside it in a fold of paper dated on the outside in his hand, squared to the edge. Anti-exemplar: Somewhere out there a man with warm hands was watching, and Wystan could almost feel him. Hunter and hunted, two sides of the same coin, bound by a thread neither could see. If only he knew how close he was.
